Outdated OpenClaw AI agent (<2026.4.23) — vulnerable to vCard/contact prompt inj AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces hosts running OpenClaw at a version below 2026.4.23 — the build where OpenClaw moved contact names, vCard fields and location labels out of the prompt body into a separate untrusted-metadata channel. Anything older is exposed to Imperva's hidden-instruction-in-shared-contact attack. Rationale: Article states 'OpenClaw shipped a fix in version 2026.4.23' for the message-object flattening flaw Imperva reported. Detection inventories OpenClaw across the estate and flags anything below 2026.4.23 — the exact version semver from the body. Sigma omitted: TVM inventory feed isn't a process_creation / file_event log source.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Host in a documented air-gapped lab that intentionally pins an older OpenClaw build
  • Slow-rolling pilot ring still on the previous LTS
  • Endpoint just imaged with a stale golden image — patch SLA hasn't elapsed yet
  • Stale inventory data where the agent uninstalled but the record hasn't aged out
  • Beta channel host that has a higher 2026.4.X-beta string the regex misreads
Suppression filter
and not (DeviceName has_any ("lab-","pilot-","qa-","staging-"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm OpenClaw is actually running on the listed hosts (process-running check, not just installed); pull the asset owner and patch ring assignment for each. Step 2 — Contain: push 2026.4.23+ via the patch system; for hosts that cannot patch immediately, disable OpenClaw's WhatsApp / contact-sharing / location ingestion connectors (the specific surfaces Imperva proved exploitable) and disable agent memory if on by default. Step 3 — Hunt: cross-check vulnerable hosts against the imperva_artifactory.com DNS / connect detection from the sibling UC — same hosts hitting both is a stronger signal of attempted PoC reuse than either alone; review the Slack/Discord/Matrix/Zalo/Teams channel-extension allowlists for any rename-to-impersonate signs (the InfoSec Write-ups disclosure of allowlist-by-display-name flaw).
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where SoftwareName has "openclaw" or SoftwareVendor has "openclaw"
| extend Parts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
| where isnull(Major) or Major < 2026
      or (Major == 2026 and Minor < 4)
      or (Major == 2026 and Minor == 4 and Patch < 23)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| order by SoftwareVersion asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SoftwareName has "openclaw" or SoftwareVendor has "openclaw"
| extend Parts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
| where isnull(Major) or Major < 2026
      or (Major == 2026 and Minor < 4)
      or (Major == 2026 and Minor == 4 and Patch < 23)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel
| order by SoftwareVersion asc
source:(osquery OR sccm OR jamf OR intune OR snipeit) AND (@software.name:(openclaw OR OpenClaw) OR @application.name:(openclaw OR OpenClaw)) AND -@software.version:(2026.4.23 OR 2026.4.24 OR 2026.4.25 OR 2026.5.* OR 2026.6.* OR 2026.7.* OR 2026.8.* OR 2026.9.* OR 2026.1[0-9].* OR 2027.* OR 2028.*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/openclaw/i
| FileVersion=*
| regex("^(2025\\.|2026\\.[0-3]\\.|2026\\.4\\.([0-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-2])$)", field=FileVersion)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, FileVersion], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="openclaw*" OR Processes.process="*openclaw*") by host Processes.process_name Processes.process_version | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=process_version "(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)" | where (major<2026) OR (major=2026 AND minor<4) OR (major=2026 AND minor=4 AND patch<23)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="openclaw*" OR Processes.process="*openclaw*") by host Processes.process_name Processes.process_version | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=process_version "(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)" | where (major<2026) OR (major=2026 AND minor<4) OR (major=2026 AND minor=4 AND patch<23)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("imperva_artifactory.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["imperva_artifactory.com"]);

   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

author: Clankerusecase

detection:

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("imperva_artifactory.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

SecurityEvent

Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse and MSNightmare) has released a new Windows BitLocker bypass dubbed GreatXML, a day after they published an exploit for Microsoft Defender. "This was an accidental discovery, it took a total of 4 hours to find this," the researcher said in a post on Blogger. "If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're

GreatXML staging: unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml dropped on Windows recovery partition AIWeaponization High
Hunts for writes of the two XML files the GreatXML PoC requires (unattend.xml at the recovery-volume root and Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml) into recovery-partition / GLOBALROOT / System Volume Information paths. Pre-boot staging is the only host-side artefact before the attacker reboots to WinRE for a BitLocker bypass. Rationale: Article names the two exact files ("unattend.xml" and "Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml") that must be staged on the recovery-partition root for GreatXML to trigger. Pairing the filenames with the GLOBALROOT/HarddiskVolume path tokens that Windows uses to expose the recovery volume keeps FPs to the legitimate WinRE servicing utilities listed in the filter. Cross-checked MITRE ATT&CK T1564.010 (Process Argument Spoofing — Hidden File System) and Microsoft Docs reagentc.exe semantics. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1564/010/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/reagentc-command-line-options
ATT&CKT1564.010 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • OEM imaging tooling (HP/Lenovo/Dell factory restore) seeding ReAgent.xml during sysprep
  • WinRE servicing during Windows Feature Updates (DISM /Apply-Image)
  • Endpoint-management tools (SCCM/Intune) re-imaging recovery partition
  • IT-built golden image deployment via MDT/Sysprep
  • Acronis/Veeam bare-metal-recovery agents touching recovery volumes
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","sedlauncher.exe","sedsvc.exe","setuphost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\$WINDOWS.~BT\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm process lineage — `InitiatingProcessFileName` and `InitiatingProcessParentFileName` should NOT be reagentc/wininit/dism/sysprep; the writing account should not be SYSTEM ($-suffix). Pull `InitiatingProcessCommandLine` and check if it is an interactive user shell (cmd/powershell/explorer). 2) Contain: isolate the device via Defender Live Response; revoke any BitLocker recovery keys cached for the device in AAD/Entra; force a TPM re-seal. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same `DeviceId` for `manage-bde.exe -off`, `reagentc.exe /boottore`, WMI `Win32_EncryptableVolume` calls in the prior 24h, and check for `mpcmdrun.exe -Scan -ScanType 3` (Defender Offline Scan) which is the documented prerequisite per the article.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\", "WindowsRE", "GLOBALROOT", "HarddiskVolume", "System Volume Information")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("reagentc.exe","wininit.exe","smss.exe","services.exe","dism.exe","sysprep.exe","setupcl.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("unattend.xml","ReAgent.xml")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Recovery\", "WindowsRE", "GLOBALROOT", "HarddiskVolume", "System Volume Information")
| where not(ActorUsername endswith "$")
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("reagentc.exe","wininit.exe","smss.exe","services.exe","dism.exe","sysprep.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
title: GreatXML BitLocker Bypass Staging - unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml on Recovery Partition
id: 7f3c2a14-8b91-4d6e-9c4a-12d5e6a8b3c1
description: Detects creation of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml on the Windows recovery partition by a non-system process — the staging step for the GreatXML BitLocker bypass disclosed by Chaotic Eclipse (June 2026).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1564.010
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\unattend.xml'
      - '\ReAgent.xml'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Recovery\'
      - 'WindowsRE'
      - 'GLOBALROOT'
      - 'HarddiskVolume'
      - 'System Volume Information'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\reagentc.exe'
      - '\wininit.exe'
      - '\smss.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
      - '\dism.exe'
      - '\sysprep.exe'
  condition: selection_name and selection_path and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\unattend.xml OR *\Unattend.xml OR *\UNATTEND.XML OR *\ReAgent.xml OR *\reagent.xml OR *\REAGENT.XML)) AND (@TargetFilename:(*\Recovery\* OR *\recovery\* OR *WindowsRE* OR *windowsre* OR *GLOBALROOT* OR *globalroot* OR *HarddiskVolume* OR *harddiskvolume* OR *"System Volume Information"*)) NOT @Image:(*\reagentc.exe OR *\ReAgentc.exe OR *\REAGENTC.EXE OR *\wininit.exe OR *\WININIT.EXE OR *\dism.exe OR *\DISM.EXE OR *\sysprep.exe OR *\SYSPREP.EXE)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\(unattend|ReAgent)\.xml$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\\\Recovery\\\\|WindowsRE|GLOBALROOT|HarddiskVolume|System Volume Information)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(reagentc|wininit|smss|services|dism|sysprep)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

ReAgentC.exe used to mount or re-image the WinRE volume from an interactive user AIExploitation High
Detects interactive use of reagentc.exe with /boottore, /setreimage, /enable, /mountre or /setosimage flags. These are the exact subcommands an attacker needs to either reboot into the WinRE state the GreatXML exploit triggers, or to rewrite the recovery image with a planted ReAgent.xml. Rationale: reagentc.exe is the documented Windows Recovery Environment configuration binary; the article's exploit requires booting into WinRE (which an attacker can force via `reagentc /boottore`) and the planted XML files must be reachable by the recovery image, which `/setreimage` and `/setosimage` re-point. Filtering out TrustedInstaller / Windows Update parents preserves legitimate servicing. Verified flag semantics against Microsoft's reagentc CLI reference. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/reagentc-command-line-options • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
ATT&CKT1218 T1490
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin running `reagentc /enable` after re-imaging a workstation
  • Helpdesk scripts that re-point WinRE following a feature update
  • Backup/recovery vendors (Acronis, Macrium) calling reagentc /setreimage
  • Dell SupportAssist or Lenovo Vantage repair flows
  • MDM-pushed remediation runbooks toggling WinRE on/off
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\$WINDOWS.~BT\"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("SupportAssist","Lenovo.Vantage","Macrium","Acronis")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full `ProcessCommandLine`, parent process, and `AccountName`; query whether the same host had a recent `unattend.xml` or `ReAgent.xml` write (UC #1) or a `mpcmdrun.exe -Scan -ScanType 3` (Defender Offline Scan — GreatXML prerequisite). 2) Contain: isolate device; if the box has BitLocker enabled, rotate the recovery key in AAD/Entra immediately and force a TPM re-seal once cleared. 3) Hunt: search the device's prior 30d for any `reagentc` activity, look for the same `AccountName` running similar commands on neighbouring hosts, and check Defender vuln-inventory for whether YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585) was patched on this host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "reagentc.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/boottore","/setreimage","/setosimage","/mountre","/enable","-boottore","-setreimage")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","sedlauncher.exe","sedsvc.exe","setuphost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\reagentc.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/boottore","/setreimage","/setosimage","/mountre","/enable","-boottore","-setreimage")
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| where not(SubjectUserName in~ ("system","local service","network service"))
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","sedlauncher.exe","sedsvc.exe","setuphost.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType

Recovery partition file write by non-SYSTEM interactive user process AIWeaponization Medium
Generalised hunt for any write into the recovery partition / GLOBALROOT / System Volume Information by a non-SYSTEM user process. Catches GreatXML variants that swap filenames as well as future recovery-partition tampering. Tier hunting because legitimate imaging tools occasionally touch these paths. Rationale: Article describes the attacker writing arbitrary files to the recovery-partition root — UC #1 catches the exact filenames, this UC catches variants and reuse of the same primitive. GLOBALROOT, HarddiskVolume, \Recovery\WindowsRE and System Volume Information\Recovery are the only canonical Windows paths exposing the recovery volume to user-mode code. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1564/010/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/windows-recovery-environment--windows-re--technical-reference
ATT&CKT1564.010 T1006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Volume Shadow Copy (VSS) snapshot rotation under System Volume Information
  • Defender writing scan logs under System Volume Information
  • Endpoint backup agents (Veeam, Acronis, Macrium) generating recovery metadata
  • Windows Setup / feature-update writing replacement WinRE files
  • BitLocker auto-unlock or recovery-key metadata writes by fvevol/services
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Veeam\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Acronis\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Macrium\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\$WINDOWS.~BT\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: review `Files` set for known PoC names (unattend.xml, ReAgent.xml) and unexpected executables (.exe/.cmd/.bat/.dll dropped under Recovery\WindowsRE). 2) Contain: if files are non-system (.xml/.exe/.cmd outside the standard WinRE manifest), isolate the host and rotate the BitLocker recovery key. 3) Hunt: correlate `InitiatingProcessAccountName` against AD/Entra for unusual session times; pivot the same `AccountName` across the fleet for repeats; check for subsequent `reagentc.exe /boottore` or `manage-bde -off` execution in the next 24h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("GLOBALROOT", @"HarddiskVolume", @"\Recovery\WindowsRE", @"System Volume Information\Recovery")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("reagentc.exe","wininit.exe","smss.exe","services.exe","dism.exe","sysprep.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","msmpeng.exe","mpcmdrun.exe","setuphost.exe")
| summarize FileCount = count(), Files = make_set(FileName, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("GLOBALROOT", "HarddiskVolume", @"\Recovery\WindowsRE", @"System Volume Information\Recovery")
| where not(ActorUsername endswith "$")
| where not(ActorUsername in~ ("system","local service","network service"))
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("reagentc.exe","wininit.exe","smss.exe","services.exe","dism.exe","sysprep.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","msmpeng.exe","mpcmdrun.exe"))
| summarize FileCount = count(), Files = make_set(TargetFileName, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath
| order by LastSeen desc

| NOT UserName=/^(SYSTEM|LOCAL SERVICE|NETWORK SERVICE)$/i

BitLocker suspend/disable via manage-bde, PowerShell Disable-BitLocker or Win32_EncryptableVolume WMI AIActions on Objectives High
Detects pre-bypass tampering with BitLocker protection state — manage-bde.exe with -off/-disable, PowerShell Disable-BitLocker/Suspend-BitLocker, or WMI Win32_EncryptableVolume method invocations. Attacker using GreatXML may first weaken BitLocker before the WinRE reboot to widen the bypass window. Rationale: Article explicitly frames GreatXML as a BitLocker bypass — attackers commonly weaken BitLocker protectors (manage-bde -off, Disable-BitLocker, Win32_EncryptableVolume.DisableKeyProtectors) before forcing the WinRE pivot. These are the documented Microsoft-supported APIs for BitLocker state change. Verified API names against Microsoft's manage-bde and BitLocker PowerShell module docs. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/manage-bde • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/bitlocker/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
ATT&CKT1562.002 T1490
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin temporarily suspending BitLocker for firmware/BIOS update
  • Helpdesk performing legitimate decryption for disk swap
  • SCCM/Intune compliance scripts toggling BitLocker state
  • Migration tools (USMT) suspending BitLocker pre-image
  • User-initiated `Suspend-BitLocker -RebootCount 1` before Windows Update of TPM driver
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("SCCM","Intune","Configuration Manager","USMT","Microsoft.Management.Services")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\CCM\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Intune Management Extension\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the `AccountName` is interactive (not a maintenance service account) and check whether a planned change window covers this time. Look for paired `unattend.xml` or `ReAgent.xml` recovery-partition writes on same host (UC #1) in prior 24h. 2) Contain: re-enable BitLocker protectors (`manage-bde -protectors -enable`) via remote command, rotate recovery key in AAD/Entra. Isolate device if no change ticket. 3) Hunt: pull `mpcmdrun.exe -Scan -ScanType 3` history (Defender Offline Scan is the GreatXML precondition) and check Defender vuln-inventory for missing YellowKey patch (CVE-2026-45585).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "manage-bde.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-off","-disable","-pause","-protectors -disable"))
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Disable-BitLocker","Suspend-BitLocker","Win32_EncryptableVolume","DisableKeyProtectors","DiscardVolumeKey"))
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "Win32_EncryptableVolume")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","sedlauncher.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\manage-bde.exe" and (CommandLine has "-off" or CommandLine has "-disable" or CommandLine has "-pause" or CommandLine has "-protectors -disable"))
   or (NewProcessName has_any (@"\powershell.exe",@"\pwsh.exe") and (CommandLine has_any ("Disable-BitLocker","Suspend-BitLocker","Win32_EncryptableVolume","DisableKeyProtectors","DiscardVolumeKey")))
   or (NewProcessName endswith @"\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "Win32_EncryptableVolume")
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| where not(SubjectUserName in~ ("system","local service","network service"))
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","sedlauncher.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
title: BitLocker Protection Disabled or Suspended (GreatXML Pre-bypass)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="manage-bde.exe" AND (Processes.process="*-off*" OR Processes.process="*-disable*" OR Processes.process="*-protectors -disable*" OR Processes.process="*-pause*")) OR (Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" AND (Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Win32_EncryptableVolume*")) OR (Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe" AND (Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Win32_EncryptableVolume*"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"(?i)SYSTEM$|\\$$") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
System utility command line referencing GLOBALROOT, HarddiskVolume or WinRE recovery paths AIExploitation Medium
Catches msiexec.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, rundll32.exe or cmd.exe executed with command lines that reference the raw recovery-partition device paths (\\?\GLOBALROOT, HarddiskVolume, System Volume Information\Recovery, \Recovery\WindowsRE). Direct-volume access via these primitives is the only way a user-mode process touches recovery files outside of reagentc.exe. Rationale: Article describes the exploit primitive as copying XML files "to the root of the recovery partition" — which user-mode code can only address through \\?\GLOBALROOT or the HarddiskVolume device-path namespace. Any scripting host or LOLBin command line that contains these path tokens is by definition direct-volume access, which is rare outside Windows servicing. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1006/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/devio/calling-deviceiocontrol
ATT&CKT1006 T1559.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin debugging WinRE via `powershell -Command 'Get-ChildItem \\?\GLOBALROOT\...'`
  • Defender researcher reproducing manage-bde flows in lab
  • Backup/imaging vendor scripts inspecting recovery contents
  • Forensic acquisition tools (FTK Imager, KAPE) reading raw volumes
  • Penetration-test exercises exercising T1006 direct-volume access
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("KAPE","FTK","AccessData","X-Ways","AXIOM")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Configuration Manager\"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("Get-ChildItem","Get-Item","Test-Path")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull full `ProcessCommandLine` and `InitiatingProcessCommandLine`; classify whether the path was read-only enumeration (`Get-ChildItem`, `dir`) or write (`Copy-Item`, `New-Item`, `cmd /c copy`). Writes are far higher fidelity. 2) Contain: if a write is confirmed against recovery paths, isolate the host via Defender Live Response and rotate the BitLocker recovery key in AAD/Entra. 3) Hunt: pivot on `AccountName` for the same user across the fleet, look for paired `reagentc.exe /boottore` or `manage-bde -off` in the next 24h, and check whether the device has the YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585) patch applied via DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("msiexec.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","cmd.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("GLOBALROOT", "HarddiskVolume", @"\Recovery\WindowsRE", @"System Volume Information\Recovery")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","sedlauncher.exe","setuphost.exe","reagentc.exe","msmpeng.exe","mpcmdrun.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\msiexec.exe",@"\powershell.exe",@"\pwsh.exe",@"\wscript.exe",@"\cscript.exe",@"\mshta.exe",@"\rundll32.exe",@"\cmd.exe",@"\regsvr32.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("GLOBALROOT", "HarddiskVolume", @"\Recovery\WindowsRE", @"System Volume Information\Recovery")
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| where not(SubjectUserName in~ ("system","local service","network service"))
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("trustedinstaller.exe","wuauclt.exe","sedlauncher.exe","setuphost.exe","reagentc.exe","msmpeng.exe","mpcmdrun.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest

| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

CloudAppEvents

AuditLogs

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

[GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48062: CodeIgniter4 has a validation bypass when uploading file extensions via `ext_in` rule

GitHub Security Advisories
2026-06-11 4 use cases 1 technique 5 kill-chain phases detected

CodeIgniter4 has a validation bypass when uploading file extensions via `ext_in` rule

CVEsCVE-2026-48062
ATT&CKT1190

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] CodeIgniter4 ext_in Bypass — PHP File Written to Public Upload Directory by Web Server
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] HTTP Access to PHP File Inside CodeIgniter4 Upload Directory (Webshell Trigger)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Webshell Execution — PHP/Web Server Process Spawning Shell After ext_in Bypass
CodeIgniter4 ext_in Bypass — PHP File Written to Public Upload Directory by Web Server AIInstallation High
Hunts the outcome of CVE-2026-48062: a web server / PHP interpreter (php-fpm, php, httpd, nginx, w3wp) writing a PHP-executable file (.php/.phtml/.phar/.phps/.inc) into a publicly-served upload path (public/uploads, public/avatar, writable/uploads, /var/www/*/uploads). This is the smoking-gun artefact of the ext_in MIME-vs-extension validation flaw described in the GHSA — the malicious shell.php with GIF-like content lands on disk. Rationale: Anchored on three article-specific strings: the affected framework's directory layout (public/, writable/uploads — explicitly named in the workarounds), the file-extension allow-list (php/phtml/phar/phps/inc — the executable types ext_in was supposed to block), and the parent process set characteristic of CodeIgniter4 deployments (php-fpm / php / httpd / nginx / w3wp). The combination of web-server-process + PHP-extension + public upload path is what makes this article-specific and not a generic webshell rule.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer install / `composer update` writing vendor PHP into the docroot under public/ (not under uploads/) — path filter excludes it
  • Static site generators or CMS plugin installers writing PHP into framework paths (admin/, themes/, plugins/) — path filter excludes it
  • Cache warmer writing compiled PHP into writable/cache or writable/sessions (not writable/uploads)
  • Image processors (Intervention/Image, Imagine) writing thumbnail files where the configured extension list accidentally lets .php through
  • CI/CD deployer (capistrano, deployer.php) syncing PHP files to /public/ during release
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has "/vendor/" and FolderPath !has "\\vendor\\" and FolderPath !has "/writable/cache" and FolderPath !has "/writable/sessions" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "composer"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the offending file path and `file` / `head -c 16` it — confirm GIF89a/GIF87a or other image magic bytes followed by `<?php` further in. Pull the parent web request from access logs (~5s window around Timestamp) to identify the source IP and the upload endpoint. Step 2 (contain): remove the file, revoke the active web session token used to upload it, and block the source IP at the WAF. If the host has been exploited, isolate it from the network. Step 3 (hunt): grep the same parent process for other recent file writes with non-image extensions in upload paths; query access logs for prior 4xx upload attempts from the same IP/UA (bypass-discovery activity); confirm the affected CodeIgniter4 install is < 4.7.3 and force-patch.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".phps" or FileName endswith ".inc"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/public/uploads","/public/avatar","/writable/uploads","/var/www","/htdocs/uploads",@"\public\uploads",@"\public\avatar",@"\writable\uploads",@"\wwwroot\uploads")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php","php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-cgi","httpd.exe","httpd","nginx.exe","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar","phps","inc")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/public/uploads","/public/avatar","/writable/uploads","/var/www","\\public\\uploads","\\public\\avatar","\\writable\\uploads","\\wwwroot\\uploads")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php","php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername

Webshell Execution — PHP/Web Server Process Spawning Shell After ext_in Bypass AIActions on Objectives High
Detects post-exploitation execution of the shell.php (or equivalent) dropped via CVE-2026-48062: a PHP interpreter or web server process (php, php-fpm, httpd, nginx, w3wp) spawning a command-line shell, recon utility, or downloader. The article confirms the bypass leads to arbitrary code execution from PHP files in web-accessible directories — this is the runtime symptom. Rationale: The article explicitly states the bypass 'may lead to arbitrary code execution'. Any execution path from a web-tier process to a shell/recon binary is the runtime smoking gun. The parent process list is anchored to the deployment binaries CodeIgniter4 actually runs under (php-fpm/php-cgi for PHP-FPM stacks, httpd/nginx as reverse proxy + execve, w3wp.exe on IIS).
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.001 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PHP cron job invoking ImageMagick / ffmpeg via shell_exec for media processing
  • phpMyAdmin / Adminer / Roundcube running shell tasks (set_time_limit, backup features) on operator-controlled hosts
  • Composer hook in a deployment pipeline running `git`, `npm`, or shell helpers under php-fpm
  • WordPress plugin auto-update invoking `tar` / `unzip` via PHP exec
  • Monitoring agents (Munin, Cacti) that run `uname`/`whoami` via a PHP web UI
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("artisan","composer.phar","wp-cli.phar","drush") and FileName in~ ("sh","bash","git","npm"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the parent process's loaded script path — for php-fpm this is in /proc/<pid>/cmdline or the web-server access log timestamp-matched to the spawn; the script path will point at the dropped shell. Pull the child command line and its child processes for the next 5 minutes. Step 2 (contain): kill the child + parent worker, isolate the host, rotate any credentials accessible to the web service account (DB password in CodeIgniter4 .env / Database.php config). Step 3 (hunt): cross-reference UC1 hits to identify other dropped PHP files on the same host, scan all CodeIgniter4 installs for unexpected files in public/uploads and public/avatar, check egress for the same RemoteIPs the child process contacted.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php","php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-cgi","httpd.exe","httpd","nginx.exe","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","python","python.exe","python3","curl","curl.exe","wget","whoami","whoami.exe","id","uname","net.exe","systeminfo.exe","nc","ncat","mshta.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildPath = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php","php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx","apache2","w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","python","python3","curl","wget","whoami","id","uname","nc","ncat","net.exe","systeminfo.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash

HTTP Access to PHP File Inside CodeIgniter4 Upload Directory (Webshell Trigger) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the access pattern that triggers the dropped webshell after a successful CVE-2026-48062 ext_in bypass: an HTTP GET or POST returning 2xx to a .php / .phtml / .phar file located under /uploads/, /avatar/, or /writable/uploads/. Under a secure deployment those paths should serve only image/static assets — a 200 response on a PHP file there means the framework has executed user-uploaded code. Rationale: The article identifies the executable extensions (PHP and 'other executable files') and the deployment shape (uploads under public web root) that make this access pattern uniquely dangerous. Hitting a .php under /uploads/ or /avatar/ with a 2xx is not a normal CodeIgniter4 traffic pattern — image-processing endpoints sit at controller routes like /index.php/avatar/show, not at /public/uploads/foo.php directly.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy timthumb.php / similar image-resize scripts deliberately deployed under /avatar/
  • File-manager UIs (elFinder, KCFinder) whose admin entry-point lives under /uploads/file_manager.php
  • CMS plugins that serve dynamic PHP from /uploads/ as a design choice (uncommon but exists)
  • Synthetic uptime monitors hitting a placeholder /uploads/healthcheck.php endpoint
  • Developer testing immediately post-deploy hitting /public/uploads/index.php
Suppression filter
| where url !endswith "/index.php" and url !contains "/avatar/timthumb" and url !contains "/uploads/file_manager"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the source IP, user-agent, and full URL including query string — webshells commonly take commands via ?cmd=, ?c=, ?0=, or POST bodies. Pull the matching DeviceFileEvent (UC1) to confirm when the file landed and which process wrote it. Step 2 (contain): block source IP at WAF/edge, remove the PHP file from the upload directory, rotate the web service account credentials and any secrets readable by it. Step 3 (hunt): for the source IP, hunt the prior 24h for failed (4xx) POSTs to /upload* endpoints (bypass discovery attempts); for the file, hunt all hosts in the org for sibling .php files in the same upload dir; confirm CodeIgniter4 version < 4.7.3 and patch.
let upload_php = dynamic([@"/uploads/",@"/avatar/",@"/writable/uploads/",@"/public/uploads/",@"/public/avatar/"]);
let php_ext = dynamic([".php",".phtml",".phar",".phps",".inc"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where csMethod in ("GET","POST")
     | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
     | where csUriStem has_any (upload_php)
     | where csUriStem has_any (php_ext)
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, srcIP=cIP, http_method=csMethod, url=strcat(csUriStem,iif(isempty(csUriQuery),"",strcat("?",csUriQuery))), status=scStatus, ua=csUserAgent, referer=csReferer),
    (ImWebSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
     | where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
     | where HttpMethod in~ ("GET","POST")
     | where Url has_any (upload_php)
     | where Url has_any (php_ext)
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, srcIP=SrcIpAddr, http_method=HttpMethod, url=Url, status=HttpStatusCode, ua=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, referer=HttpRequestHeaderReferer))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")

| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling

ImFileEvent

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
